card.title: Laravel framework hot-path speedup (Str, Collection, Blade, hashing)

spike_plan.kill_if: Timing CV above 10% on the same host, or the combined known changes give under 1.2x on the whole benchmark set.
spike_plan.pass_if: Suite runs green at head; at least three of four hot paths show a >10% gain from known changes; benchmark CV under 5% across runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone laravel/framework at v13.38.0 and check the PHP version it requires; install that PHP CLI.
Run composer install and the PHPUnit suite on head; record pass/fail counts per test.
Check whether head already uses xxh128 for cache/view keys (grep the source only for this spike); if so, the base must revert it.
Write micro-benchmarks for Str helpers, a Collection pipeline, a Blade compile of a template set, and cache-key hashing; run each 5 times on 8 cores.
Compute median and coefficient of variation per benchmark; confirm the hot paths are measurably slow and the timing is stable.
Apply the xxh128 change alone and measure the speedup on the hashing benchmark; confirm PHPUnit still passes.
Repeat the three-run determinism check on the full benchmark set.

v1.summary: The seed's hashing lever is real but public: PR #45371 (xxh128 switch) merged 2022-12-20, so the reference is recallable and the base must revert it, and the claimed S and later perf commits were not confirmed. No hard kill, but Band is capped at 3 without dated evidence and the 4h tier looks short for four levers, so 8h is proposed.

v2.note: The anchor PR #45371 (xxh128) was merged in 2022 and is already in the v13 head, so the slow base would be an artificial revert, and the agent knows the upstream fix (lookup direct). The 'later merged perf commits' for Str, Collection and Blade are not identified and S is unmeasured (weak reference). The hashing lever is a one-line swap. PHP micro-benchmarks under gVisor are also noise-prone.
